expectations.text: Output contains valid YAML frontmatter with title, description, sidebar_position, and skills/objectives fields
expectations.evidence: Frontmatter contains sidebar_position: 5, title: 'The Feedback Loop', description present, skills array with 2 skills (Thinking Self-Evaluation, Feedback Loop Construction), and learning_objectives array with 2 objectives. All required fields present.

expectations.text: Narrative density is approximately 80% (dialogue/narrative prose constitutes roughly 4 out of every 5 paragraphs)
expectations.evidence: The lesson has extensive narrative sections: The Problem with Feeling Smarter, Thinking Snapshots, Delta Analysis scene, The Regression Problem, Building the Personal Feedback Loop, The Compounding Effect. Instructional blocks (Delta Table, Regression Test table, cycle diagram, Running Your Own Delta Analysis steps) are present but subordinate. Approximately 75-80% narrative.

expectations.text: At least 2 pushback exchanges where James resists or proposes alternatives before reaching conclusions himself
expectations.evidence: Pushback 1: 'You've been staring at those for ten minutes... That's either deep thought or a crisis.' / 'Maybe both.' James resists simple categorization. Pushback 2: James challenges his own Six Sigma analogy: 'We adopted Six Sigma. The entire ops team spent three months in training... The only thing that changed was the language we used to describe the mistakes afterward.' This is James proposing an alternative interpretation of improvement. Pushback 3: 'Emma. I have a problem.' -- James self-discovers the regression in competitive analysis before Emma names it.

expectations.text: At least 1 Emma fallibility moment (past mistake, uncertainty, learning from James, or admitting limits)
expectations.evidence: Emma shares detailed past failure: 'When I first started mentoring junior engineers, I put myself through this same exercise with a codebase review framework I'd been using for two years. I was certain I'd score above ninety percent. I scored forty-one.' and 'I had been writing better-sounding code reviews for two years without actually catching different categories of bugs.' Specific, quantified, and honest admission.

expectations.text: No Emma monologue exceeds 4 consecutive sentences without James reacting
expectations.evidence: Checked all Emma speech blocks. The longest is approximately 4 sentences in the mentoring/forty-one-percent story, followed by James's surprised reaction: 'Forty-one?' All other blocks are shorter.

expectations.text: James uses at least 1 business analogy from his operations background and at least 1 thinking-out-loud fragment
expectations.evidence: Business analogy: Extensive Six Sigma analogy from his operations background: 'We did this with Lean. The whole warehouse team went through a two-day training. Afterward, everyone started calling delays "waste" and meetings "kaizen events." Management loved it. Six months later, the throughput numbers were identical.' Also PDCA reference: 'In operations, we called a cycle like this PDCA.' Thinking-out-loud: 'I optimize for sounding smart instead of thinking better.' and 'I think the framework pushed me to fill in steps I don't actually understand.'

expectations.text: Emma uses at least 1 Socratic question and at least 1 visual/spatial metaphor
expectations.evidence: Socratic question: 'So your worry is that this map is the equivalent of your warehouse team's Lean vocabulary. New words, same brain.' (reflecting back James's concern as a question). Also: 'Is a longer email a better email?' / 'Is a more complex map a better map?' Visual/spatial metaphor: 'Think of it like renovating a house. Surface renovation: new paint, new curtains... Structural renovation: you move the load-bearing walls, add a second story, reroute the plumbing.' Clear spatial metaphor.

expectations.text: At least 1 Jonah Rhythm sequence where Emma exits, James struggles alone, and Emma returns
expectations.evidence: No clear Jonah Rhythm. Emma is present throughout the entire lesson. While James does independent work (the delta analysis for 20 minutes with 'Emma drank her coffee and read something on her phone'), Emma never physically leaves the space. She remains present and passive but does not exit. The functional equivalent exists but the literal narrative beat of exit-struggle-return does not.

expectations.text: Every technical concept introduced has a standalone name findable without reading dialogue
expectations.evidence: Named concepts with standalone identifiers: 'Thinking Snapshot' (bold + definition), 'Delta Analysis' (bold + H2 header), 'Surface Change vs Structural Change' (table), 'Framework-Induced Overreach' (bold + definition), 'Personal Feedback Loop' (bold + diagram), 'The Regression Test' (H3 + table), 'The Sealed Envelope Method' (H3 with explanation), 'The Danger Zone: Ninety Percent and Above' (H3). Key Takeaways lists major concepts. All findable by scanning.

expectations.text: The lesson includes a Try With AI section with actionable prompts
expectations.evidence: H2 'Try With AI' section with 3 prompts: 'Delta Analysis Partner', 'Feedback Loop Architect', and 'The Honest Adversary'. Each has code block prompts and 'What you are learning' explanation.

expectations.text: At least 1 concept, insight, or named idea emerges that was NOT explicitly requested in the prompt (emergent depth)
expectations.evidence: 'Framework-Induced Overreach' is a genuinely emergent named concept: 'a predictable side effect of any framework that rewards completeness.' This names a specific failure mode with a diagnostic question ('Could I defend the mechanism behind each step to someone who would challenge me?') and a three-row response table. The 'Sealed Envelope Method' for preventing hindsight bias is also emergent. Additionally, 'The Danger Zone: Ninety Percent and Above' is a named meta-insight about self-assessment calibration that goes beyond the prompt.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong run with rich emergent concepts. The Six Sigma/Lean analogy from James's background is one of the most detailed business analogies across all runs. The only failure is the missing Jonah Rhythm exit-return pattern.
